source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), General Directorate of Agriculture, Department of Agricultural Extension — 'បច្ចេកទេសដាំដំណាំឪឡឹក' (Watermelon Cultivation Techniques), 2017.
text:
After basal fertilizer application at land preparation, the book gives a top-dressing (side-dressing) fertilizer schedule applied progressively as the crop grows, timed at roughly 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50 days after transplanting/sowing, for a planting density referenced in the table at about 220 plants per plot area.

At around 10 days after planting, a light application of NPK compound fertilizer (20-20-15) is combined with a small amount of urea (46-0-0), applied close to the plant base (about 10 centimeters from the stem). At around 20 days, NPK (20-20-15) is applied together with a potassium fertilizer (0-0-60), again close to the plant. From around 30 days through 40 and 50 days after planting, further rounds of NPK (20-20-15) combined with potassium (0-0-60) are applied, with the fertilizer placement moved progressively further from the stem (out to about 25 centimeters) as the root system expands outward with plant growth. Fertilizer is generally applied in a shallow trench or band around the plant and then lightly covered with soil, followed by irrigation to help it dissolve and reach the root zone.

Note: the exact per-application kilogram totals printed in the source table were difficult to read with full confidence from the scanned image and should be verified against the original document by a human before being used as precise dosage recommendations; the fertilizer types, approximate timing (10/20/30/40/50 days), and general application method described above were clearly legible.
